purpose: Name the single human-facing EscapeHatch product release identity, classify competing version-like surfaces, and bind Git tags to exact validated commits without replacing commit/artifact identity.

scheme_justification.why: Installable product surfaces exist (browser extension now; Microsoft Store / Play Store / local-web adapters planned). Users and operators need MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH meaning for upgrade risk. Companion upgrade invariants require distribution upgrades that preserve user-owned state; SemVer expresses product-surface compatibility separately from schema/protocol versions.
scheme_justification.not_calver: No fixed release cadence owns product identity today.
scheme_justification.not_monotonic_only: A bare build counter would hide whether an upgrade is breaking for installable clients.
evidence_to_reconsider: If installable distribution is abandoned and only private operator tooling remains, reconsider a monotonic build sequence.
If cadence becomes the primary public identity and compatibility is wholly owned by schema versions, reconsider CalVer plus independent schema contracts.

cutover.rule: Ratify the existing browser extension manifest version as the first authoritative product release. Pre-cutover contract 'version: 1' integers and '*.v1.json' schema labels remain schema/protocol versions only and were never product release authority. No Git tags or GitHub Releases existed at cutover; do not rename, reuse, or decrement released versions after this point.

pre_authority_labels.surface: contracts and harness schema version integers / escapehatch-*/v1 strings

synchronized_mirrors.notes: MV3 extension package version must equal VERSION.

surface_classification.surface: Git commit SHA / CI run / artifact hash
contracts/*/version integers and escapehatch-*/vN schema_version strings

bump_matrix.judgment_gate: A human or reviewed change record must classify each accepted change as one of major|minor|patch|none. Automation then applies the highest selected bump deterministically. Automation must not invent the classification.

rules.notes: Removes or changes shipped product behavior such that existing installs/operators must take non-automatic action, or breaks a documented product compatibility promise.
Adds capability without requiring a breaking migration for existing installs.
Fixes incorrect behavior without adding a feature or breaking compatibility.
No product release bump; docs may ship on main without a release tag.
No bump unless user-visible behavior or a mirrored product surface changes.
Advance the independent schema/protocol version; do not pretend it is a product release.
Optional prerelease suffixes (for example 1.1.0-rc.1) are allowed only before that exact X.Y.Z is tagged as final. Never reuse a finalized X.Y.Z.
Ship from a maintenance line only by tagging a new patch derived from that line; do not reuse or decrement versions.
Backports receive a new patch on the maintained MAJOR.MINOR line; identity remains the new tag plus commit SHA.

consumers: future Microsoft Store / Play Store / local-web companion adapters
operators validating repository releases against Git tags and commit SHAs
user-owned career-state / preference stores (compatibility owned by schema versions, not product SemVer alone)

product_semver_means.MAJOR: Breaking change to installable product behavior, config, CLI, or required operator/user migration.

product_semver_does_not_mean: application-companion / assist-session / preference-cache contract compatibility (owned by those schema versions)
freshness; only commit SHA / tagged commit / artifact hash proves exact identity
breaking_change_requirements: CHANGELOG entry under the new MAJOR describing the break
migration or deprecation notes appropriate to the affected surface
schema breaks use independent schema version advancement plus migration evidence
compatibility.rollback: Redeploy or restore a previously tagged commit/artifact. Never decrement VERSION or reuse a released number.
compatibility.withdrawn_release: Preserve the historical tag and CHANGELOG identity; document replacement or yank status in CHANGELOG rather than deleting history.

release_mechanics.publication_boundary: GitHub Release creation, browser-store submission, and Microsoft/Play store submission remain downstream credentials/environment gates after repository tag identity is valid.
